title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Economic primitives (automation vs augmentation on Claude.ai)
measure: % of ~1m sampled Claude.ai conversations (one week) classed as automation (directive + feedback loop) vs augmentation (task iteration, validation, learning)
finding: Automation went from 41% (Jan 2025, restated from 43%) to 49% (Aug 2025) to 45% (Nov 2025); no later split appears in any report text.
limits: one vendor; own classifier, changed between waves; one-week samples; product mix shifts

title: Anthropic Economic Index report, September 2025 (directive share)
measure: % of sampled Claude.ai conversations classed 'directive' (whole task delegated with minimal back-and-forth)
finding: Directive share rose from 27% (Dec 2024–Jan 2025) to 39% (Aug 2025), then fell 7 points to 32% (Nov 2025, per the Jan 2026 report).
limits: one vendor; classifier changed; the fall to 32% is often omitted when the rise is quoted

title: Anthropic Economic Index: first-party API automation share (Sep 2025, Jan 2026, Mar 2026 reports)
measure: % of 1P API transcripts (businesses calling Claude from their own software) classed as automation
latest_value: about 75% (Nov 2025); 'decreased sharply' by Feb 2026, no figure in text
finding: Business API traffic is mostly automation (77% Aug 2025, three-quarters Nov 2025), and the March 2026 report says automation then 'decreased sharply' in API data (appendix figure only).
limits: programmatic by nature; no 2026 number in text; one vendor

title: Anthropic Economic Index September 2025 report, footnote 4 (classifier re-run)
measure: automation share of the same Aug 2025 Claude.ai sample under two classifier models (Sonnet 4 vs Sonnet 3.7)
finding: Re-classifying the August 2025 sample with the older model gave 45% automation instead of 49%, a gap as large as the later 'easing' to 45%; the rise in directive use held under both models.
limits: method note; later waves' classifier not stated in text

title: Anthropic Economic Index September 2025 report (country usage vs automation)
measure: automation vs augmentation share by country against Claude usage per capita, controlling for task mix
finding: As Claude usage per head rises, countries shift from automation-focused to augmentation-focused use, even after controlling for task mix.
limits: cross-section; one vendor; authors call it counter-intuitive and needing more research

title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Cadences
measure: AI autonomy (1–5 scale) by product, Apr 10–Jun 10 2026; automation share of survey-linked users (mid-May to early Jun 2026)
finding: Claude Code sessions score 0.37 points more autonomous than chat on a 1–5 scale (a median blog post takes one prompt in Claude Code against 13 rounds in chat); users with more automated sessions are more optimistic about their jobs; women's automation share is 7.3 points lower.
limits: no aggregate automation split in text; survey-linked users only; one vendor

title: Anthropic Economic Index data release 2026-06-26 (monthly aggregates), data documentation
measure: collaboration_bucket_automation_pct and directive/feedback-loop shares by calendar month, Claude.ai (chat + Cowork) and 1P API, global and by country
latest_value: values not read (April and May 2026 in a 219 MB CSV)
finding: The June 2026 release publishes monthly automation and directive shares for April and May 2026, which would update the site's Nov 2025 figure, though the report text gives none.
limits: scope now includes Cowork (a break); values must be pulled by hand; Hugging Face blocked from this environment

title: Measuring AI agent autonomy in practice
measure: Claude Code auto-approve share and interrupt rate by user experience; 99.9th-percentile turn duration (Oct 2025–Jan 2026)
finding: Experienced users auto-approve over 40% of sessions against about 20% for new users (a cross-section), yet interrupt more (9% vs 5% of turns); the longest 0.1% of turns grew from under 25 to over 45 minutes, then 'declined somewhat' after mid-January.
limits: cross-section, not a trend; coding only; one vendor

title: Measuring AI agent autonomy in practice (public API tool calls)
measure: % of 998,481 sampled public-API tool calls with a human in the loop; % irreversible; domain mix
finding: At most 73% of agent tool calls have a human in the loop (Anthropic calls it an upper bound), 0.8% look irreversible, and software engineering is nearly half of calls.
limits: one snapshot; upper bound; classifier-inferred

title: How AI is transforming work at Anthropic
measure: per-transcript maximum run of Claude Code tool calls without human input; human turns per transcript (200,000 transcripts, Feb vs Aug 2025); survey of 132 staff
finding: The longest unbroken run of agent actions rose from 9.8 to 21.2 per transcript and human turns fell from 6.2 to 4.1 in six months, yet most staff say they can fully delegate only 0–20% of their work.
limits: AI lab's own engineers, the most favourable setting; two points

title: Agentic coding and persistent returns to expertise
measure: share of planning vs execution decisions made by user or Claude in ~400,000 Claude Code sessions (Oct 2025–Apr 2026)
finding: Users made about 70% of planning decisions but only 20% of execution decisions, and use shifted towards end-to-end agentic work over the seven months, with debugging's share nearly halved.
limits: one vendor; coding only; no time series for the decision split

title: How People Use ChatGPT (NBER w34255)
measure: % of sampled consumer ChatGPT messages classed Asking / Doing / Expressing
finding: 'Doing' fell from about half of messages (Jul 2024) to 34.6% (late Jun 2025) as non-work use grew from 53% to over 70%; among work messages, nearly 56% were Doing.
limits: one study; consumer plans only; no 2026 update found

title: How agents are transforming work (summary of 'The shift to agentic AI: evidence from Codex')
measure: Codex share of output tokens (OpenAI staff); growth in Codex users since Aug 2025; % of sampled users requesting tasks estimated over 1 h / 8 h (Dec 2025–May 2026)
finding: Inside OpenAI the agent (Codex) went from under 10% of the average worker's tokens (to Aug 2025) to over 85% (Jun 2026); in May 2026, 70.2% of sampled individual users asked for a task estimated at over an hour.
limits: vendor's own staff and users; tokens not tasks; task lengths model-estimated

title: Working with AI: Measuring the Applicability of Generative AI to Occupations
measure: overlap between O*NET work activities in the user's goal and those the AI performs, 200k Bing Copilot conversations (Jan–Sep 2024)
finding: In 40% of conversations the activities the AI performed did not overlap with the user's goal, and the AI completed its own activities less fully than it advanced users' goals, i.e. it mostly assisted rather than did the work.
limits: one product, 2024 only; consumer Copilot; Microsoft's own data

title: AI in the Enterprise: How People Use M365 Copilot Chat
measure: task mix in ~5.5m enterprise Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat sessions
finding: Writing dominates enterprise Copilot Chat, and use is moving away from 'chat as search' towards content and communication work; no delegation share is given in the abstract.
limits: abstract only read; no automation measure; Microsoft's own data

title: Sundar Pichai shares news from Google Cloud Next 2026
measure: % of new code at Google 'AI-generated and approved by engineers' (CEO statements)
finding: Google's stated share rose from over a quarter (Oct 2024) to 50% ('last fall', 2025) to 75% (Apr 2026); the last two are on Google's own Cloud Next post.
limits: no published method; one firm that sells AI; irregular statements

title: Who is using AI to code? Global diffusion and impact of generative AI
measure: % of Python functions in public GitHub commits classified as AI-written, by country, 2019–2024 (30m+ commits, 170,000 developers)
finding: By end-2024 about 29% of US Python functions were AI-written (Germany and France 23–24%, India 20%), with newcomers using AI for 37% of code against 27% for the most experienced.
limits: Python and public GitHub only; detector-based; ends 2024; journal version (Science) not checked

title: State of the Coding Agent Market (Oct 2026) and Coding Agents trends tracker
measure: share of public GitHub pull requests carrying a coding-agent mark; weekly agent-marked PR counts by agent
latest_value: 19.4% of all public PRs (Aug 2026); 32.5% of 1,999 most recent PRs (to 27 Sep 2026)
finding: About one in five public pull requests in August 2026 carried an AI-agent mark, and Claude Code alone went from about 7,700 marked PRs a week (Sep 2025) to 1.6m (week to 28 Sep 2026).
limits: commercial tracker; counts are floors; attribution defaults change; public repos only; recent-PR samples small

title: State of Code Developer Survey (press release, 8 Jan 2026)
measure: self-reported % of committed code that is AI-generated; % of developers who always check AI-assisted code before committing (1,100+ developers)
finding: Developers say AI accounts for 42% of committed code (65% expected by 2027), but only 48% always check AI-assisted code before committing and 96% do not fully trust it.
limits: self-report; vendor of code-checking tools; fieldwork dates not stated; one-off

title: Agents on a leash: agentic AI remains mostly monitored at work
measure: % of developers using AI agents at work (any frequency; daily); oversight practices
finding: Agent use at work rose from 31% (2025 Developer Survey) to 59% (April 2026 pulse), daily use from 14% to 37%, yet 63% rarely or never let agents run fully on autopilot and 60% block unapproved system changes.
limits: different samples (annual survey vs 1,100-person pulse); self-report; developers only; daily figures read from chart

title: The results of the 2026 Developer Survey are here
measure: % of AI-using developers using coding agents; AI use by development stage (30,000+ respondents)
finding: Among developers who use AI, 66% use coding agents, but only 20% use AI for deploying, operating or troubleshooting production systems.
limits: subset bases; full results not read; self-selected sample

title: Future of Work with AI Agents: Auditing Automation and Augmentation Potential across the U.S. Workforce (WORKBank)
measure: worker desire for automation and preferred Human Agency Scale level for 844 O*NET tasks in 104 occupations (1,500 workers, Jan–May 2025)
finding: Workers were positive about automating 46.1% of their tasks, but equal partnership (H3) was the most-wanted level in 47 of 104 occupations; the ten occupations most keen on automation make up only 1.26% of Claude usage.
limits: one-off; preferences not behaviour; online recruitment

title: Human Agency Scale (H1–H5)
measure: five-level scale of how much human involvement a task should keep
finding: Offers a five-level, provider-neutral scale that could serve as the shared hand-over definition the site says is missing.
limits: level definitions not re-read this session

title: The Anthropic Economic Index (collaboration patterns)
measure: five collaboration patterns: directive and feedback loop (automation); task iteration, validation and learning (augmentation)
finding: Defines hand-over as a chat-level request pattern, not a decision handed to AI, which is the concept slip the red team flagged.
limits: definition confirmed via June 2026 report and data documentation, not this page

title: The state of AI (2026)
measure: % of respondents whose organisation is scaling AI agents (1,719 respondents, 4 May–8 Jun 2026)
latest_value: 40% of large firms, 22% of smaller ones (2026)
finding: Large organisations (over $1bn revenue) scaling AI agents rose from 27% to 40% in a year; smaller ones stayed near 22%; about two in ten overall.
limits: executive self-report; 'scaling' loosely defined; adoption more than hand-over

title: AI Quarterly Pulse Survey (agent deployment)
measure: % of US firms with revenue of $1bn+ that have deployed at least some AI agents (130–204 executives per quarter)
finding: Reported deployment went 11%, 11%, 33%, 42%, 26%, 55%, 53% from Q4 2024 to Q2 2026: rising, but with a 16-point one-quarter drop.
limits: small samples; wording widened in Q3 2026; consulting firm selling AI services

title: State of Agent Engineering
measure: % of respondents with AI agents in production (1,340 responses, 18 Nov–2 Dec 2025)
finding: 57% of respondents had agents in production, up from 51% a year earlier; 59.8% use human review to evaluate them.
limits: self-selected; 63% tech sector, half under 100 staff; agent-tooling vendor

title: Gartner Predicts Over 40% of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by End of 2027
measure: forecast shares of work decisions and enterprise software involving agentic AI
finding: Gartner forecasts at least 15% of day-to-day work decisions made autonomously by agentic AI by 2028 (0% in 2024), agentic AI in 33% of enterprise software by 2028, and over 40% of agentic AI projects cancelled by end-2027.
limits: analyst forecast; no method published

title: Artificial intelligence in UK financial services – 2024
measure: % of AI use cases with some automated decision-making, semi-autonomous, fully autonomous; % of firms using AI (118 firms)
latest_value: 55% of use cases some automated decision-making; about 2% fully autonomous (2024)
finding: 75% of UK financial firms used AI (58% in 2022); 55% of use cases involved some automated decision-making but only about 2% were fully autonomous.
limits: use cases not decisions; survey roughly every two years, decision split asked in 2024 only as far as checked; page inconsistent on the 2%

title: DSA Transparency Database
measure: % of platform content-moderation statements of reasons flagged as fully automated decisions, rolling 180 days
finding: 43% of 3.94 billion platform moderation decisions in the last six months were fully automated.
limits: 'automated' is not always AI; share driven by platform mix; no published trend

title: Automated Transparency: A Legal and Empirical Analysis of the Digital Services Act Transparency Database
measure: automated detection and decision flags by platform, 131m statements of reasons, 19–28 Nov 2023
finding: TikTok, Google Shopping, AliExpress and Google Maps made mostly or wholly automated decisions, while X, LinkedIn and Booking.com reported none, so the EU-wide share mostly reflects which platforms dominate volume.
limits: ten-day window; self-declared flags

title: 73% of Employers Say They Use AI in Hiring Decisions
measure: % of 1,000 US hiring managers saying AI automatically rejects candidates before human review
finding: 65% of hiring managers said AI rejects some candidates before any human review, and 14% said it rejects more than half of applicants.
limits: career-site marketing survey; no fieldwork dates; read via trade press

title: 7 in 10 US consumers use AI to shop
measure: % of 2,000 US adults who have used AI to complete a purchase
finding: 30% said they had used AI to complete a purchase, but the survey does not say whether an agent bought on their behalf; a separate Cognizant/Oxford Economics study found 75% unwilling to let AI make high-value purchases alone.
limits: marketing-agency survey; definitions vague; read via trade press

title: Remote Labor Index leaderboard
measure: % of real paid freelance projects completed by an AI agent at client-acceptable quality
finding: The best automation rate rose from 2.5% or less for 2025 models (e.g. GPT-5.2, Manus 1.5) to 21.25% for the newest entry, so the ceiling on what can be handed over is rising fast.
limits: capability, not use; entry dates not shown; belongs with the capability stop

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks
measure: length of software task (human time) AI agents complete with 50% success
finding: Context only: the task length agents can finish alone has doubled roughly every four to seven months, setting what could be handed over.
limits: capability not use; software only; not re-read this session

title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
measure: share of occupations' tasks exposed to LLMs (O*NET)
finding: About 80% of US workers could have at least 10% of tasks affected and 19% at least half; exposure, not hand-over.
limits: potential exposure; OpenAI co-authors; context only

title: Occupational, industry, and geographic exposure to artificial intelligence: A novel dataset and its potential uses
measure: AI Occupational Exposure index (overlap of AI applications with job abilities)
finding: Ranks occupations by potential AI exposure; context for where hand-over could occur, not a measure of it.
limits: pre-generative AI; potential only; not re-read

title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
measure: theory of incremental substitution of human participation in economy, culture and states
finding: Predicts that tasks and decisions shift to AI step by step, each sensible locally, weakening the human participation that keeps systems aligned.
limits: theory; not re-read this session

title: The AI Fluency Index
measure: % of 9,830 multi-turn Claude.ai chats (20–26 Jan 2026) in which users check facts or question reasoning
finding: Users checked facts in 8.7% of chats and checked less when the output was a polished artifact; the nearest thing to a review rate, framed as a baseline to repeat.
limits: conversations not people; one vendor; figures from earlier note, not re-read

title: 2025: The State of Generative AI in the Enterprise
measure: % of enterprise and start-up AI deployments that qualify as true agents (495 respondents, Nov 2025)
finding: Only 16% of enterprise and 27% of start-up deployments qualified as true agents, so much 'agent' adoption is still assisted workflows.
limits: venture investor survey; figures from earlier note, not re-read
